blind_spots.blind_spot: Sells 'real-time' undersea data while the physics of their own platform makes the link the binding constraint
blind_spots.operator_reality: A drifting node in the upper 400 m has no RF path until it surfaces; when it does, it gets a satellite slot measured in hundreds of bytes and minutes of visibility. 'Dense, real time upper ocean data' from a distributed sub-surface constellation is latency in hours and payloads in bytes — which means detection and summarization must happen on the node, not shoreside. That is the same architecture decision as the crowd-detection startup that streamed 30 fps into a link with room for one frame every five seconds; discovering it after the Phase II is a redesign, not a tuning pass.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their anchor customers in the site's framing are climate modelers and aquaculture, who accept batch delivery and never test the latency claim; the word 'real-time' has cost them nothing so far.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Dense, real time upper ocean data is a crucial component of understanding climate change and improving forecasting, especially of extreme weather events.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Data-as-a-Service delivery assumes a commercial pipe into a customer who lives on a classified network
blind_spots.operator_reality: An MDA or ISR consumer receives data inside an accredited enclave. A vendor-hosted feed reaching that watch floor needs an authorized delivery path (IL5 or higher), CUI handling for the collection, and an ITAR review of subsea sensor performance parameters — and the sensor-performance data itself is likely export-controlled the moment it is characterized against a threat. None of that is a contract line the DaaS pricing model contains.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The business model was designed to avoid selling hardware, which is exactly the right commercial instinct and exactly the thing that pushes the accreditation burden onto a 17-person company with no security engineering function visible.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Data As A Service — Tell us what data you need, where, and for how long. We'll take care of the rest.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Reusability is stated as a product virtue with no recovery, refurbishment, or shipboard-handling reality attached
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'From expendability to reusability' means someone recovers the nodes. In a Navy context that is a deck evolution off a ship or small boat in sea state, a crew that must be trained on the handling procedure, and lithium batteries that need shipboard-carriage safety approval before they are allowed aboard at all. Add a spares and refurbishment pipeline and a depot decision. Expendable sensors sidestep every one of those gates; reusable ones inherit all of them, and the approval timeline for battery carriage alone routinely outruns a Phase II.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Reusability is a cost-per-data-point argument, and cost-per-data-point is the metric the whole company is organized around — the sustainment cost lands on the operator's side of the ledger where it never shows up in their model.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: from episodic sampling to continuous observing, from expendability to reusability, and from human-assisted to autonomous sensing
